question: A mechanism that can split the power of a propeller shaft to the rear axle and produce variation in the speed of rear wheels when the vehicle takes a turn is called a/an:
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Differential Unit**

__
 
• A differential unit is a mechanical device used in vehicles to split the power from the propeller shaft to the rear axle and allow variation in the speed of the rear wheels when the vehicle takes a turn. It is an integral part of the drivetrain system in automobiles, ensuring efficient power delivery and smooth turning by accommodating the different rotational speeds of the wheels.

**Working Principle:**

 
• When a vehicle turns, the wheels on the outer side of the turn travel a greater distance compared to the wheels on the inner side. This difference in distance requires the wheels to rotate at different speeds. The differential unit facilitates this by splitting the torque from the propeller shaft and transmitting it to the rear axle, allowing each wheel to rotate independently at the required speed. Inside the differential, gears work together to ensure the proper distribution of power and variation in rotational speed.

**Components:**

 
• **Ring Gear:** Connected to the propeller shaft and drives the differential gears.
 
• **Pinion Gear:** Engages with the ring gear to transfer power.
 
• **Spider Gears:** Allow the wheels to rotate at different speeds during turns.
 
• **Side Gears:** Connected to the axle shafts and receive power from the spider gears.
 
• **Housing:** Encases the differential unit and holds all components together.

**Advantages:**

 
• Improved handling and maneuverability by accommodating different wheel speeds during turns.
 
• Ensures smooth power delivery to the rear wheels.
 
• Reduces wear and tear on tires by preventing skidding during cornering.

**Disadvantages:**

 
• Complex design, requiring precise manufacturing and assembly.
 
• Higher maintenance cost compared to simpler drivetrain components.
 
• Loss of traction in some situations, especially with open differentials.

**Applications:**

 
• Used in all types of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and SUVs.
 
• Essential in rear-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles.
 
• Found in heavy-duty vehicles for smooth operation on uneven terrain.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 1:** Differential unit

The differential unit is specifically designed to split the power from the propeller shaft and allow variation in the speed of the rear wheels during turns. This functionality is critical for ensuring smooth cornering and preventing unnecessary strain on the drivetrain components.

To further understand the analysis, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 2:** Integral Unit

This option is incorrect as an integral unit does not perform the functions required for splitting power or allowing variation in wheel speeds. The term "integral unit" typically refers to other components in mechanical systems, such as integrated assemblies, but not the differential function.

**Option 3:** Torque Convertor

A torque convertor is a type of fluid coupling used in automatic transmissions to transfer rotational power from the engine to the drivetrain. It is unrelated to the function of splitting power to the rear axle or allowing variation in wheel speeds during turns.

**Option 4:** Automatic Clutch Unit

An automatic clutch unit is a component in vehicles with automated manual transmissions, designed to engage and disengage the clutch without manual input. It does not perform the function of splitting power or managing wheel speed variations during turns.
